families.notes: Behind λόγος, λέγω (say) and every English -logy.
The same family gives both “cosmos” and “cosmetic”.
Shares a family with ἀγαπάω, to love.
Behind γραφή (writing, Scripture) and every English -graphy.

words.notes: 2nd declension. The -ος ending marks nominative singular; the accusative is λόγον.
Every attested ending here begins with omicron, so the corpus invariant looks like αἰωνιο-. The standard analysis is stem αἰωνι- with the 2nd-declension -ος ending.
The -ω ending marks 1st person singular present; -ει marks 3rd person.

passages.translation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
passages.notes: θεόν and θεὸς are the same word in different cases — accusative after πρός, then nominative. Only the ending moves.

passages.translation: In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
passages.notes: τῶν ἀνθρώπων is genitive plural — “of the men”. The article declines with its noun.

passages.translation: And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
passages.notes: φαίνει is present — “shines”, not “shone”. κατέλαβεν is aorist, a single completed act in the past.

passages.translation: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ.
passages.notes: Three genitives in a row: “the beginning OF the gospel OF Jesus Christ”. Greek stacks them where English needs repeated “of”.
